cards.title: Keyword Research Workflow with Google Keyword Planner and Trends
cards.summary: Build a per-page keyword set (one main, two supporting) using Google Keyword Planner volume/CPC data and Google Trends related queries.
cards.use_when: Planning keyword targets before editing a homepage, product page, collection, or blog post's SEO fields.
steps: Open Google Ads and go to Tools > Planning > Keyword Planner (account required to see data). Set language and country to match your target market.
Enter a seed term describing your product category (example: 'homemade soap'); read monthly search volume, competition level, and CPC range to gauge commercial value.

Pick one main keyword and two supporting keywords per page. The source's demo chose 'homemade soap' as main (1,000–10,000 monthly searches, high competition) with lower-volume, more specific terms as support.
Use Google Trends related searches (optionally with the Glimpse Chrome extension) to surface adjacent queries, then paste them back into Keyword Planner to check volume.
Test a query in Google search and harvest autocomplete predictions as candidate keywords, then validate them in Keyword Planner.
Optionally paste a competitor's URL into Keyword Planner's 'start with website' option to see which keywords their pages already rank for, and choose gaps to target.
Assign each page a distinct keyword set based on that page's content; don't reuse the same set across all products.
caveats: Volume/CPC shown are estimates from Google's tools, not guarantees.
Higher-end tools (Ahrefs, Semrush) give richer intent and country data but cost more; Keyword Planner is the free fallback.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Separate Informational vs Transactional Search Intent
cards.summary: Match keywords to intent so product and collection pages target buyers while blog posts absorb informational searches.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether a keyword belongs on a product/collection page, a blog post, or nowhere in your catalog.
steps: Classify each keyword: informational (e.g., 'how to make homemade soap') vs transactional (e.g., 'homemade soap for sale', 'homemade soap near me').
Route transactional keywords to product and collection pages, where the visitor can immediately buy.
Route informational keywords to blog posts and guide pages that link internally to the relevant products.
When using tools with explicit intent labels (e.g., Semrush), use them to confirm intent instead of guessing.
Favor keywords with buying intent when the page's goal is revenue; use informational terms to build topical authority and feed internal links to money pages.
caveats: Intent labels are tool heuristics and can be wrong; spot-check the live SERP if in doubt.
Informational traffic converts far less directly — judge it on assisted discovery, not last-click sales.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Edit Global Store SEO: Homepage Title and Meta Description
cards.summary: Set the site-wide homepage title and meta description so the homepage ranks for your main brand/category keyword.
cards.use_when: Setting or fixing the homepage listing that appears in Google results for brand and category searches.
steps: In Shopify admin, go to Online Store > Preferences and find the Search engine listing section.
Write a title that includes the main keyword; respect the 70-character field limit. The source's demo used 63 characters with the main keyword plus supporting terms.
Write a meta description containing supporting keywords and optionally a call to action; keep it accurate to the brand voice.
Optionally draft candidates with ChatGPT, then edit so they genuinely represent your brand — avoid overly broad keywords that don't match your niche.
Save, then verify by searching the keyword in Google to see how your listing renders.
caveats: The title/description you write here is the homepage listing only; each product, collection, page, and blog post has its own listing fields.
Field character limits may change in Shopify's interface — verify current limits.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Enforce a Single H1 Tag Per Page
cards.summary: Ensure every page has exactly one H1 so Google can identify the page's main topic.
cards.use_when: Auditing a theme or custom section for heading structure on product, collection, homepage, or custom-built pages.
steps: Inspect the page in the browser and check which element carries the H1. On Shopify's Dawn theme, the homepage H1 is typically the logo; on collection pages the collection title is the H1; on product pages the product title is the H1.
Check custom sections a developer or you built — they sometimes introduce an extra H1.
If two H1s exist, demote one to H2 or lower so only the intended main title remains H1.
After fixing, re-inspect to confirm only one H1 remains on every page type.
caveats: Theme behavior differs; the logo-as-H1 behavior is stated for Dawn and may not hold for all themes — verify in your theme.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Write SEO Product Titles from Specs Using Keyword Data
cards.summary: Turn raw product specs into a keyword-rich but readable product title and description.
cards.use_when: Rewriting vague product names (e.g., 'Sweet Honey Bomb') that don't tell Google or shoppers what the product is.
steps: Copy the product's specs/description into ChatGPT and ask for candidate high-volume keywords relevant to those specs.
Validate those keywords in Google Keyword Planner; discard ones with weak volume or poor relevance.
Feed the validated keyword list back into ChatGPT asking for title options; pick the best and include at least the main keyword plus a supporting keyword.
Paste the title into the Shopify product Title field and save.

For the description, ask ChatGPT to write from the specs, instructing it to weave in the researched keywords but keep the text natural (not obviously AI-generated). Aim for at least 100 words; the source says 300–400 words is ideal for product copy.
Format the description — bold key points, add images inside it, and adjust theme title font size in the customizer if the longer title breaks layout.
Edit the result so it matches your brand voice before publishing.
caveats: AI output must be reviewed for accuracy and brand fit; don't publish unedited.
Longer titles may require theme typography adjustments to avoid layout breakage.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Image SEO: Alt Text, File Names, and Formatting
cards.summary: Optimize every product/media image with descriptive alt text and a keyword-based file name.
cards.use_when: Preparing product photos, banners, and gallery media before or after uploading to Shopify.
steps: Write alt text that combines the target keyword, the product name, and a visual descriptor: the source's example is 'summer fragment bath bomb purple frontal' (keyword + product + color + angle).
Reuse the alt text to rename the actual image file so the file name is descriptive rather than a string of numbers/gibberish.
Work through every image in the product's media gallery, then go to Content > Files and fix the alt text and file names for the store's media library.
Optionally verify by inspecting the image on the storefront to confirm the descriptive URL is live.
caveats: Alt text also serves accessibility for visually impaired shoppers — describe the image honestly, don't just stuff keywords.
Compress images before upload (keep files under 2MB) to avoid hurting page speed.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Write Product Meta Descriptions That Earn Clicks
cards.summary: Craft a roughly 160-character product meta description focused on click appeal rather than keyword density.
cards.use_when: Filling the per-product Search engine listing meta description field in Shopify.
steps: Take the product description and ask ChatGPT to produce a ~160-character search engine listing meta description.
Review and edit for accuracy, brand voice, and a compelling reason to click; the source says the meta description is less about keywords and more about enticing the click.
Paste it into the product's Search engine listing meta description field and save.
If you have a large catalog and manual editing isn't feasible, use an SEO app to bulk-generate, and hand-edit top sellers.
Use the listing preview to confirm how the title and description will render in Google results.
caveats: Very large catalogs may not be practical to edit manually — prioritize high-value pages or use bulk tooling.
Excerpts can also be left auto-derived if they already read well.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Clean URL Handles and Enable 301 Redirects
cards.summary: Shorten product/collection URL handles and keep the automatic redirect checked to avoid losing bookmarked traffic.
cards.use_when: Editing a product or collection URL handle in the Search engine listing preview.
steps: In the product/collection Search engine listing section, edit the URL handle to remove filler words and reflect the product/collection name (e.g., use the title with grammar and special characters stripped out).
Before saving, confirm the checkbox that automatically creates a redirect from the old URL to the new one is checked.
Save. Bookmarked old URLs then forward to the new page instead of returning a 404.
Repeat for collections and any page whose handle you change; the handle should contain the keywords from the title so Google understands the page.
caveats: If the redirect box is unchecked, existing bookmarks and external links break with 404 errors and you lose those visits.
Redirect handling in Shopify's UI may vary by version — verify the checkbox location.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Optimize Collection Pages Without Pushing Products Down
cards.summary: Add keyword-rich collection titles and descriptions while keeping the product grid above the fold.
cards.use_when: Improving a collection page (e.g., 'Bath') that currently has no descriptive content.
steps: Do keyword research for the collection and write a descriptive title that names the products it contains (the source's example reframes a vague 'Bath' into a title describing the scent/type of products).
Write a collection description of roughly 100–400 words containing the right keywords so Google can crawl and understand the page.
In the Shopify theme editor, move the collection description below the product grid if you want products visible first — keep the text on the page regardless.
Set the collection's Search engine listing title and meta description, and update the URL handle to remove filler words.
Confirm the automatic redirect checkbox is checked so the old collection URL forwards to the new one.
Repeat for every collection on the store.
caveats: The source notes that many merchants skip collection descriptions because they push products down; moving the block resolves the tension.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Optimize Pages and Blog Posts, Then Interlink Them
cards.summary: Apply the same title/description/handle process to all pages and posts, and build internal links to spread crawl coverage.
cards.use_when: Extending SEO beyond products and collections, and setting up internal linking between blog content and products.
steps: For every Shopify page and blog post, fill in the title (containing the main keyword plus optionally a secondary), the content/description (with keywords and real value), and the Search engine listing meta description and handle.
Publish new content regularly: the source recommends at least two posts a month, ideally one per week, researched through Keyword Planner and relevant to what you sell.
Add internal links wherever there is a natural opportunity — for example, link from a blog post or benefits page directly to the relevant product in the body content.
Link broadly across pages, posts, and products so that crawling one page reveals the next, helping Google discover more pages faster.
caveats: Posting frequency is the source's recommendation, not a documented ranking threshold — treat it as a practical cadence.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Mobile-Friendliness and Page Speed Checks for Ranking
cards.summary: Verify mobile rendering and diagnose load-speed issues Google uses to rank stores.
cards.use_when: Auditing a theme before or after launch for mobile and speed problems that suppress rankings.
steps: In Chrome, right-click > Inspect, toggle device view, and preview as a device (e.g., iPhone 12 Pro); check that nothing overflows the screen, images aren't distorted, and all content is reachable. In Safari, use Develop > Enter Responsive Design mode.
Run Google PageSpeed Insights on your store URL and read the field data — the source notes these graphs reflect the past 28 days, so fixes won't show there immediately.

Compress all images before upload (keep under 2MB; a page should total roughly 2MB, and an uncompressed 1.4MB image is a problem). The source recommends a free compression service; an SEO app can also bulk-optimize.

Do NOT lazy-load above-the-fold images (e.g., a product hero or homepage banner) — these are typically the Largest Contentful Paint element and lazy-loading them worsens LCP. Other off-screen images can use loading=lazy.
Audit installed apps: third-party app code is out of your control and can slow the store; uninstall anything unused (you can reinstall later) and keep only apps that bring real value.
Re-run the speed test and fix the flagged issues you can act on.
caveats: Most modern Shopify themes are mobile-friendly out of the box, so mobile checks often confirm rather than fix.
PageSpeed field data lags ~28 days — don't expect instant improvement in the graphs.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Add Rich Snippets (FAQ and Product Schema)
cards.summary: Enable structured data so search results show FAQs, ratings, prices, and availability.
cards.use_when: Wanting extra visible SERP real estate for product, FAQ, or article content.
steps: Add a lightweight, accessible FAQ answering genuine pre-purchase questions; do not justify it with promised FAQ rich results.
Add the schema either via custom code (the source references a guide) or via an SEO app that generates FAQ and review schema.
For app-generated snippets, toggle the desired type on (e.g., FAQ, product grid, image) and run the app's built-in test to confirm the snippet is correctly injected.
Monitor Search Console for rich result eligibility and errors.
caveats: Structured data markup requirements and Google's supported rich result types change over time — verify current specs before investing in custom code.
Rich snippets make listings larger and more clickable but don't guarantee ranking.
Use store FAQs to answer shopper questions. Do not promise Google FAQ rich results or treat FAQ markup as a ranking requirement; verify current search feature support.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Submit the Shopify XML Sitemap to Search Console
cards.summary: Point Google at your sitemap after setting your primary domain.
cards.use_when: Finalizing technical SEO setup after optimizing pages so Google can crawl and index them.
steps: First confirm the correct domain is primary: Settings > Domains, set your custom (non-myshopify) domain as primary. The source stresses doing this BEFORE submitting the sitemap so Google crawls the right URLs.
View your sitemap at yourstore.com/sitemap.xml and copy the URL.
In Google Search Console, create/link the property for your site, then go to Indexing > Sitemaps and submit the sitemap URL.
Google will begin crawling and indexing the site; if you changed the primary domain afterward, submit a new sitemap.
caveats: Sitemap path and Search Console navigation can change — verify current interface.
Submitting a sitemap requests crawling; it does not guarantee indexing or ranking.
Sitemaps support discovery; submission does not guarantee crawling, indexing or rankings.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Set Brand Information for Search and Sales Channels
cards.summary: Fill in the Shopify brand tab so Google, Facebook, and other channels represent you accurately.
cards.use_when: Setting up or refreshing store branding that feeds external sales channels and search appearances.
steps: Locate the brand settings tab (the source used Shopify Sidekick to find the link); add logos, colors, and brand identity assets.
Ensure the brand data is consistent, since other sales channels like Facebook and Google pull this information to represent you online.
Revisit when adding new channels or products so listings stay consistent.
caveats: The exact location of brand settings may shift in Shopify admin — verify in your account.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Build Backlinks and Recurring Content for Authority
cards.summary: Grow authority through external links and consistent publishing, which the source frames as what Google rewards.
cards.use_when: Planning off-page SEO and content cadence to lift overall ranking potential.
steps: Pursue backlinks from authoritative sites: partner with people who run large websites, or work with influencers who can mention and link to your store in their articles.
Treat authority as transferable — being featured on a high-authority site passes some of that trust to your store.
Publish new content regularly; the source recommends at least 2 posts/month and ideally weekly.
Research each planned post with Keyword Planner and write on topics close to what you sell and that your customers want to learn about.
For each post, set the title with the main (and optionally secondary) keyword, put the keywords in the content, add a click-worthy meta description, and include a keyword-bearing URL handle.
Use an SEO app to track existing backlinks and find broken links to fix.
caveats: The posting-frequency suggestion is the presenter's opinion, not a documented Google requirement.
Backlink effects are slow and depend on the linking site's authority.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Audit Existing Rankings to Fix Wasted Content
cards.summary: Review which keywords you already rank for and correct pages ranking for irrelevant or zero-volume terms.
cards.use_when: Doing a periodic SEO review to redirect content toward terms that actually drive traffic.
steps: Use an SEO app's 'analyze my keywords' feature (the source shows SEOAnt) to list keywords you currently rank for.
Flag pages ranking for keywords with no search volume or no commercial relevance (the source notes blog posts often do this).
Adjust that content or page to target more useful keywords instead.
Optionally monitor competitor sites by entering their URL to track the keywords they rank for and how they change over time, then adapt strategies that fit your budget.
caveats: Competitor-tracking and keyword-analysis features may sit behind paid app tiers.
Prioritize pages with business value; not every irrelevant ranking needs fixing.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Deciding Whether to Automate Shopify SEO with an App
cards.summary: Weigh manual on-page SEO against app-based automation for image compression, scores, snippets, and keyword research.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to execute SEO at scale across a large catalog.
steps: Assess scope: manual editing of every product/collection/page listing is impractical for large catalogs, so prioritize manual work on high-value pages.

Use an SEO app for bulk tasks the source demonstrated: compressing all product/collection images, generating per-page SEO scores with actionable fix pointers, injecting rich snippets without code, and finding/fixing broken links.

Treat app SEO scores as prioritization guides, not goals: the demo raised a product page from bad to 91 by adding a keyword-bearing H2, then to 94 by adding in-description images and a keyword in the meta description without hitting 100.
Use the app's built-in keyword-research and rank-tracking tools as a partial replacement for Keyword Planner/Ahrefs.
Try the free tier for a small store; upgrade only if the workload justifies it.
caveats: The app recommendation is promotional in the source; the presenter discloses a discount code. Evaluate features and pricing yourself and verify the current interface.
Score targets are app-specific heuristics, not Google ranking rules.
Third-party apps add load and can affect page speed.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx
